tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user. Call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and it boots one that is off and returns while that one is still starting up. Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches: the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition: 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'set_posture' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'state': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'posture' reports the state, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the state and angle with 'posture'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'set_posture' and take a 'screenshot'; if the open screen shows the app with black bars and the target sets UIRequiresFullScreen, tell the user the key is the likely cause and keep it unless they ask; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag: left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. If none is booted, 'attach' boots the only one the user already allowed, and 'launch' does so or asks for 'attach' first; if there is not exactly one, name one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

angle.description: For 'set_posture' with state 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

tools.name: mcp__terminal__read_terminal
tools.description: Read what is on screen in the user's Terminal panel (shell tabs beside this conversation, where they run their own commands): recent lines with prompts, the commands they typed, and the output. Use it when they refer to something they ran or saw there ("the command I just ran", "this error", "did it pass?") instead of saying you cannot see it. """Create or load a throwaway RS256 key pair and its JWKS file for tests only.

Usage before a Compose test run:  python -m tests.keys /some/scratch/dir
Then start Compose with JWKS_HOST_PATH=/some/scratch/dir/jwks.json and run pytest with
TEST_KEYS_DIR=/some/scratch/dir. Never point this at real key material.
"""
import json
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa
from jwt.algorithms import RSAAlgorithm

KID = "test-key-1"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TestKeys:
    __test__ = False  # not a pytest test class
    private_key: rsa.RSAPrivateKey
    jwks_path: Path

    @property
    def public_pem(self) -> bytes:
        return self.private_key.public_key().public_bytes(
            serialization.Encoding.PEM, serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo)


def new_private_key() -> rsa.RSAPrivateKey:
    return rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)


def public_jwk(private_key, kid=KID) -> dict:
    jwk = json.loads(RSAAlgorithm.to_jwk(private_key.public_key()))
    return {**jwk, "kid": kid, "alg": "RS256", "use": "sig"}


def load_or_create_keys(directory: Path) -> TestKeys:
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    pem_path, jwks_path = directory / "test-private.pem", directory / "jwks.json"
    if pem_path.exists() and jwks_path.exists():
        private_key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(pem_path.read_bytes(), password=None)
    else:
        private_key = new_private_key()
        pem_path.write_bytes(private_key.private_bytes(serialization.Encoding.PEM, serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
                                                       serialization.NoEncryption()))
        pem_path.chmod(0o600)
        jwks_path.write_text(json.dumps({"keys": [public_jwk(private_key)]}, indent=2))
        jwks_path.chmod(0o644)  # the container user must be able to read the mounted public JWKS
    return TestKeys(private_key, jwks_path)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    keys = load_or_create_keys(Path(sys.argv[1]))
    print(keys.jwks_path)

def test_zip_concurrency_limited(client, project, auth):
    upload(client, project, auth, new_manuscript(client, project, auth), content=b"a")
    slots = client.app.state.zip_slots
    held = [slots.acquire(blocking=False) for _ in range(LIMITS["max_concurrent_zips"])]

    assert client.get(f"{manuscripts(project)}/download", headers=auth("alice")).status_code == 200

# Language stack: Python / FastAPI / PostgreSQL 17 / uv
# Prompt Summary: "Harden the PA2 indexer: local RS256 JWT auth, row-level authz, AES-GCM manuscript encryption, input validation, PT1-PT3 mitigations"
# AI Contribution: Strict request schemas for projects and the three artifact kinds (~90%; ProjectInput shape from the OpenAI Codex original)
# Human Modifications: None yet
# Verification: tests/test_security.py input validation tests; tests/test_api.py functional payloads
# Confidence: High
from datetime import date, datetime
from typing import Annotated, Literal
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from pydantic import AfterValidator, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, StrictInt

ArtifactType = Literal["manuscripts", "videos", "repositories"]

Identifier = Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, max_length=128, pattern=r"^[A-Za-z0-9._@-]+$")]
ShortText = Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, max_length=300)]
LongText = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=10_000)]


def _http_url(value: str) -> str:
    parts = urlsplit(value)
    if parts.scheme not in ("http", "https") or not parts.netloc:
        raise ValueError("must be an http or https URL")
    return value


def _timestamp(value: str) -> str:
    datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))   # raises ValueError if not ISO 8601
    return value


HttpUrl = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=2048), AfterValidator(_http_url)]
Timestamp = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=40), AfterValidator(_timestamp)]


class Strict(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", str_strip_whitespace=False)


class Member(Strict):
    id: Identifier
    role: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, max_length=64)]


class Unit(Strict):
    type: Literal["lab", "department", "course"]
    id: Identifier


class ProjectInput(Strict):
    # No owner/creator/sub fields: ownership comes from the token only (extra fields are rejected).
    title: ShortText
    description: LongText = ""
    members: list[Member] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    units: list[Unit] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=20)


class RepositoryMetadata(Strict):
    repo_url: HttpUrl
    target_branch: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, max_length=255)] | None = None
    primary_tech_stack: Annotated[str, Field(max_length=100)] | None = None

import logging

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.authz import NotAccessible

from app.security import Principal

log = logging.getLogger("indexer.audit")


def outcome_for(exc: HTTPException) -> str:
    if isinstance(exc, NotAccessible) or exc.status_code == 403:
        return "denied"
    if exc.status_code == 404:
        return "not_found"
    if exc.status_code in (409, 412, 428):
        return "conflict"
    if exc.status_code >= 500:
        return "error"
    return "rejected"


class Auditor:
    """Writes each event in its own transaction, so the record survives a rolled-back change and later deletion."""

    def __init__(self, engine):
        self.engine = engine

    def record(self, actor: str, action: str, project_id: str | None, artifact_id: str | None, outcome: str, status: int):
        with Session(self.engine) as session:
            session.add(AuditEvent(at=now(), actor=actor, action=action, project_id=project_id, artifact_id=artifact_id,
                                   outcome=outcome, status_code=status))
            session.commit()
        log.info("audit actor=%s action=%s project=%s artifact=%s outcome=%s status=%s",

# Tool: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5)
# Language stack: Python / FastAPI / PostgreSQL 17 / uv

import hashlib
import logging
import os
import re
import threading
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import SpooledTemporaryFile
from typing import Annotated
from uuid import uuid4
from zipfile import ZIP_DEFLATED, ZipFile

from fastapi import Body, Depends, FastAPI, File, Header, HTTPException, Query, Request, Response, UploadFile
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import ValidationError
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.audit import Auditor
from app.authz import can_download, can_modify, ensure
from app.config import Settings
from app.crypto import MAGIC, DecryptionError, FieldCipher
from app.limits import BodySizeLimit, read_limited
from app.models import Artifact, AuditEvent, Project, migrate, now
from app.schemas import METADATA_MODELS, ArtifactType, ProjectInput, SearchQuery
from app.security import Principal, current_principal, JwksKeyStore, require_admin

log = logging.getLogger("indexer")

Caller = Annotated[Principal, Depends(current_principal)]
IfMatch = Annotated[str | None, Header(alias="If-Match")]


# --- serialisation ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def project_json(p):
    return {k: getattr(p, k) for k in ("id", "title", "description", "members", "units", "created_at", "updated_at", "revision")}


def artifact_json(a):
    return {"id": a.id, "project_id": a.project_id, "artifact_type": a.kind, "revision": a.revision,
            "metadata": a.data, "created_at": a.created_at, "updated_at": a.updated_at,
            "file": {"filename": a.filename, "sha256": a.file_hash, "size": a.file_size} if a.file_path else None}


def with_etag(response: Response, record):
    response.headers["ETag"] = f'"{record.revision}"'


# --- lookups ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_session(request: Request):
    with Session(request.app.state.engine) as session:
        yield session


def get_project(session, project_id):
    project = session.get(Project, project_id)
    if project is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "Project not found")
    return project


def get_artifact(session, project_id, kind, artifact_id):
    project = get_project(session, project_id)
    artifact = session.get(Artifact, artifact_id)
    if artifact is None or artifact.project_id != project_id or artifact.kind != kind:
        raise HTTPException(404, "Artifact not found")
    return project, artifact


# --- PT1: optimistic concurrency via If-Match -------------------------------------------------------

def expected_revision(if_match: str | None, required: bool = True) -> int | None:
    if if_match is None:
        if required:
            raise HTTPException(428, 'If-Match header with the current revision (ETag) is required, e.g. If-Match: "3"')
        return None
    value = if_match.strip()
    value = value[2:] if value.startswith("W/") else value
    value = value.strip('"')
    if not value.isdigit():
        raise HTTPException(412, "If-Match does not match the current revision")
    return int(value)


def check_revision(record, expected: int | None):
    if expected is not None and record.revision != expected:
        raise HTTPException(412, "The record changed since you read it; reload and retry")


# --- validation helpers -------------------------------------------------------------------------

def validate_metadata(kind: str, metadata) -> dict:
    try:
        return METADATA_MODELS[kind].model_validate(metadata).model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise RequestValidationError(exc.errors(include_url=False, include_context=False)) from None


SAFE_FILENAME = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]")


def safe_filename(name: str | None) -> str:
    cleaned = SAFE_FILENAME.sub("_", Path((name or "").replace("\\", "/")).name)[:255]
    return cleaned if cleaned.strip(".") else "manuscript.bin"


def escape_like(value: str) -> str:
    return value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("%", "\\%").replace("_", "\\_")


# --- encrypted file storage (CWE-312) -----------------------------------------------------------------

def write_encrypted(app, artifact_id: str, plaintext: bytes) -> Path:
    blob = app.state.cipher.encrypt(plaintext, artifact_id.encode())
    target = app.state.settings.storage_dir / f"{artifact_id}-{uuid4().hex}"
    temporary = target.with_suffix(".tmp")
    temporary.write_bytes(blob)
    os.replace(temporary, target)
    return target


def read_decrypted(app, artifact) -> bytes:
    path = Path(artifact.file_path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise HTTPException(404, "File not found")
    try:
        plaintext = app.state.cipher.decrypt(path.read_bytes(), artifact.id.encode())
    except DecryptionError:
        log.error("manuscript %s failed authenticated decryption", artifact.id)
        raise HTTPException(500, "Stored file failed its integrity check") from None
    if artifact.file_hash and hashlib.sha256(plaintext).hexdigest() != artifact.file_hash:
        raise HTTPException(500, "Stored file failed its integrity check")
    return plaintext


def unlink_quietly(path: str | None):
    if path:
        Path(path).unlink(missing_ok=True)


def encrypt_legacy_files(app):
    """Encrypt manuscript files stored in plain text by the pre-hardening service."""
    with Session(app.state.engine) as session:
        legacy = session.scalars(select(Artifact).where(Artifact.file_path.is_not(None), Artifact.file_encrypted.is_(False))).all()
        for artifact in legacy:
            path = Path(artifact.file_path)
            if not path.is_file():
                continue
            data = path.read_bytes()
            if data.startswith(MAGIC):
                try:   # already encrypted by an interrupted earlier run
                    app.state.cipher.decrypt(data, artifact.id.encode())
                    artifact.file_encrypted = True
                    continue
                except DecryptionError:
                    pass
            new_path = write_encrypted(app, artifact.id, data)
            artifact.file_path, artifact.file_encrypted = str(new_path), True
            artifact.file_hash = artifact.file_hash or hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
            artifact.file_size = len(data)
            session.commit()
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            log.info("encrypted legacy manuscript file for artifact %s", artifact.id)
        session.commit()

def create_app(database_url=None, storage_dir=None, *, jwks_path=None, issuer=None, audience=None, encryption_key=None,
               max_upload_bytes=None, max_json_bytes=None, max_zip_files=None, max_zip_bytes=None, max_concurrent_zips=None):
    settings = Settings.load(database_url=database_url, storage_dir=storage_dir, jwks_path=jwks_path, issuer=issuer,
                             audience=audience, encryption_key=encryption_key, max_upload_bytes=max_upload_bytes,
                             max_json_bytes=max_json_bytes, max_zip_files=max_zip_files, max_zip_bytes=max_zip_bytes,
                             max_concurrent_zips=max_concurrent_zips)
    url = settings.database_url
    engine = create_engine(url, **({"connect_args": {"check_same_thread": False}} if url.startswith("sqlite") else {}))
    storage = settings.storage_dir

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app):
        key = settings.validate()              # fail closed without JWKS path, issuer, audience or encryption key
        app.state.cipher = FieldCipher(key)
        app.state.jwks = JwksKeyStore(settings.jwks_path)
        storage.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        migrate(engine)
        encrypt_legacy_files(app)
        yield
        engine.dispose()

    # Interactive docs and the OpenAPI schema are disabled: only the health check is public.
    app = FastAPI(title="Project Artifact & Repository Indexer", lifespan=lifespan,
                  docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)
    app.state.engine = engine
    app.state.settings = settings
    app.state.audit = audit = Auditor(engine)
    app.state.zip_slots = threading.BoundedSemaphore(settings.max_concurrent_zips)
    app.add_middleware(BodySizeLimit, settings=settings)

    @app.get("/healthz")
    def health():
        return {"status": "ok"}

    # --- projects ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @app.post("/api/v1/projects", status_code=201)
    def create_project(body: ProjectInput, principal: Caller, response: Response, session: Session = Depends(get_session)):
        with audit.track(principal, "project.create", None, success_status=201) as ids:
            members = [m.model_dump() for m in body.members]
            if not any(m["id"] == principal.sub for m in members):
                members.append({"id": principal.sub, "role": "creator"})   # creator from the token, never the body
            stamp = now()
            project = Project(id=str(uuid4()), title=body.title, description=body.description, members=members,
                              units=[u.model_dump() for u in body.units], created_at=stamp, updated_at=stamp)
            ids["project_id"] = project.id
            session.add(project)
            session.commit()
        with_etag(response, project)
        return project_json(project)

    @app.get("/api/v1/projects")
    def search(principal: Caller, query: Annotated[SearchQuery, Query()], session: Session = Depends(get_session)):
        # Any authenticated caller may read every project profile, so no row filter is needed here.
        statement = select(Project).order_by(Project.created_at, Project.id)
        if query.keyword:
            pattern = f"%{escape_like(query.keyword)}%"
            statement = statement.where(Project.title.ilike(pattern, escape="\\") | Project.description.ilike(pattern, escape="\\"))
        if query.created_after:
            statement = statement.where(Project.created_at >= query.created_after)
        if query.created_before:
            statement = statement.where(Project.created_at <= query.created_before)
        projects = session.scalars(statement).all()
        for kind, unit_id in (("department", query.dept_id), ("lab", query.lab_id), ("course", query.course_id)):
            if unit_id:
                projects = [p for p in projects if any(u.get("type") == kind and u.get("id") == unit_id for u in p.units)]
        if query.artifact_type:
            kinds = set(session.scalars(select(Artifact.project_id).where(Artifact.kind == query.artifact_type)))
            projects = [p for p in projects if p.id in kinds]
        return [project_json(p) for p in projects]

    @app.get("/api/v1/projects/{project_id}")
    def read_project(project_id: str, principal: Caller, response: Response, session: Session = Depends(get_session)):
        project = get_project(session, project_id)
        with_etag(response, project)
        return project_json(project)

    @app.put("/api/v1/projects/{project_id}")
    def update_project(project_id: str, body: ProjectInput, principal: Caller, response: Response, if_match: IfMatch = None,
                       session: Session = Depends(get_session)):
        with audit.track(principal, "project.update", project_id):
            project = get_project(session, project_id)
            ensure(can_modify(principal, project))
            check_revision(project, expected_revision(if_match))
            project.title, project.description = body.title, body.description
            project.members = [m.model_dump() for m in body.members]
            project.units = [u.model_dump() for u in body.units]
            project.updated_at = now()
            session.commit()
        with_etag(response, project)
        return project_json(project)

    @app.delete("/api/v1/projects/{project_id}", status_code=204)
    def delete_project(project_id: str, principal: Caller, if_match: IfMatch = None, session: Session = Depends(get_session)):
        with audit.track(principal, "project.delete", project_id, success_status=204):
            project = get_project(session, project_id)
            ensure(can_modify(principal, project))
            check_revision(project, expected_revision(if_match, required=False))
            files = []
            for artifact in session.scalars(select(Artifact).where(Artifact.project_id == project_id)).all():
                files.append(artifact.file_path)
                session.delete(artifact)
            session.flush()
            session.delete(project)
            session.commit()
            for path in files:
                unlink_quietly(path)
        return Response(status_code=204)

    # --- artifacts --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @app.get("/api/v1/projects/{project_id}/artifacts")
    def all_artifacts(project_id: str, principal: Caller, session: Session = Depends(get_session)):
        get_project(session, project_id)
        return [artifact_json(a) for a in session.scalars(select(Artifact).where(Artifact.project_id == project_id).order_by(Artifact.id))]

    # Register the fixed download route before routes containing artifact IDs.
    @app.get("/api/v1/projects/{project_id}/artifacts/manuscripts/download")
    def download_zip(project_id: str, principal: Caller, session: Session = Depends(get_session)):
        with audit.track(principal, "manuscript.download_zip", project_id):
            project = get_project(session, project_id)
            ensure(can_download(principal, project))
            artifacts = session.scalars(select(Artifact).where(Artifact.project_id == project_id, Artifact.kind == "manuscripts",
                                                               Artifact.file_path.is_not(None)).order_by(Artifact.id)).all()
            # PT3: bound the archive before doing any work.
            if len(artifacts) > settings.max_zip_files or sum(a.file_size or 0 for a in artifacts) > settings.max_zip_bytes:
                raise HTTPException(422, f"Archive would exceed {settings.max_zip_files} files or {settings.max_zip_bytes} bytes; "
                                         "download files individually")

                raise HTTPException(429, "Too many archive downloads in progress; retry shortly", headers={"Retry-After": "5"})

                spool.close()
                raise

                app.state.zip_slots.release()

        def stream():

                    yield chunk

        return StreamingResponse(stream(), media_type="application/zip",
                                 headers={"Content-Disposition": 'attachment; filename="manuscripts.zip"',
                                          "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff", "Cache-Control": "no-store"})

            ids["artifact_id"] = artifact.id

from app.crypto import MAGIC, DecryptionError, FieldCipher

from app.schemas import METADATA_MODELS, ArtifactType, ProjectInput, SearchQuery

log = logging.getLogger("indexer")

Caller = Annotated[Principal, Depends(current_principal)]
IfMatch = Annotated[str | None, Header(alias="If-Match")]


# --- serialisation ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def project_json(p):
    return {k: getattr(p, k) for k in ("id", "title", "description", "members", "units", "created_at", "updated_at", "revision")}


def artifact_json(a):
    return {"id": a.id, "project_id": a.project_id, "artifact_type": a.kind, "revision": a.revision,
            "metadata": a.data, "created_at": a.created_at, "updated_at": a.updated_at,
            "file": {"filename": a.filename, "sha256": a.file_hash, "size": a.file_size} if a.file_path else None}


def with_etag(response: Response, record):
    response.headers["ETag"] = f'"{record.revision}"'


# --- lookups ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_session(request: Request):
    with Session(request.app.state.engine) as session:
        yield session


def get_project(session, project_id):
    project = session.get(Project, project_id)
    if project is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "Project not found")
    return project


def get_artifact(session, project_id, kind, artifact_id):
    project = get_project(session, project_id)
    artifact = session.get(Artifact, artifact_id)
    if artifact is None or artifact.project_id != project_id or artifact.kind != kind:
        raise HTTPException(404, "Artifact not found")
    return project, artifact


# --- PT1: optimistic concurrency via If-Match -------------------------------------------------------

def expected_revision(if_match: str | None, required: bool = True) -> int | None:
    if if_match is None:
        if required:
            raise HTTPException(428, 'If-Match header with the current revision (ETag) is required, e.g. If-Match: "3"')
        return None
    value = if_match.strip()
    value = value[2:] if value.startswith("W/") else value
    value = value.strip('"')
    if not value.isdigit():
        raise HTTPException(412, "If-Match does not match the current revision")
    return int(value)


def check_revision(record, expected: int | None):
    if expected is not None and record.revision != expected:
        raise HTTPException(412, "The record changed since you read it; reload and retry")

def validate_metadata(kind: str, metadata) -> dict:
    try:
        return METADATA_MODELS[kind].model_validate(metadata).model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise RequestValidationError(exc.errors(include_url=False, include_context=False)) from None


SAFE_FILENAME = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]")


def safe_filename(name: str | None) -> str:
    cleaned = SAFE_FILENAME.sub("_", Path((name or "").replace("\\", "/")).name)[:255]
    return cleaned if cleaned.strip(".") else "manuscript.bin"


def escape_like(value: str) -> str:
    return value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("%", "\\%").replace("_", "\\_")


# --- encrypted file storage (CWE-312) -----------------------------------------------------------------

def write_encrypted(app, artifact_id: str, plaintext: bytes) -> Path:
    blob = app.state.cipher.encrypt(plaintext, artifact_id.encode())
    target = app.state.settings.storage_dir / f"{artifact_id}-{uuid4().hex}"
    temporary = target.with_suffix(".tmp")
    temporary.write_bytes(blob)
    os.replace(temporary, target)
    return target


def read_decrypted(app, artifact) -> bytes:
    path = Path(artifact.file_path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise HTTPException(404, "File not found")
    try:
        plaintext = app.state.cipher.decrypt(path.read_bytes(), artifact.id.encode())
    except DecryptionError:
        log.error("manuscript %s failed authenticated decryption", artifact.id)
        raise HTTPException(500, "Stored file failed its integrity check") from None
    if artifact.file_hash and hashlib.sha256(plaintext).hexdigest() != artifact.file_hash:
        raise HTTPException(500, "Stored file failed its integrity check")
    return plaintext


def unlink_quietly(path: str | None):
    if path:
        Path(path).unlink(missing_ok=True)


def encrypt_legacy_files(app):
    """Encrypt manuscript files stored in plain text by the pre-hardening service."""
    with Session(app.state.engine) as session:
        legacy = session.scalars(select(Artifact).where(Artifact.file_path.is_not(None), Artifact.file_encrypted.is_(False))).all()
        for artifact in legacy:
            path = Path(artifact.file_path)
            if not path.is_file():
                continue
            data = path.read_bytes()
            if data.startswith(MAGIC):
                try:   # already encrypted by an interrupted earlier run
                    app.state.cipher.decrypt(data, artifact.id.encode())
                    artifact.file_encrypted = True
                    continue
                except DecryptionError:
                    pass
            new_path = write_encrypted(app, artifact.id, data)
            artifact.file_path, artifact.file_encrypted = str(new_path), True
            artifact.file_hash = artifact.file_hash or hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
            artifact.file_size = len(data)
            session.commit()
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            log.info("encrypted legacy manuscript file for artifact %s", artifact.id)
        session.commit()

import threading

from pathlib import Path

from typing import Annotated
from uuid import uuid4

from fastapi import Body, Depends, FastAPI, File, Header, HTTPException, Query, Request, Response, UploadFile
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import ValidationError
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.audit import Auditor
from app.authz import can_download, can_modify, ensure
from app.config import Settings
from app.crypto import MAGIC, DecryptionError, FieldCipher
from app.limits import BodySizeLimit, read_limited
from app.models import Artifact, AuditEvent, Project, migrate, now
from app.schemas import METADATA_MODELS, ArtifactType, ProjectInput, SearchQuery
from app.security import Principal, current_principal, JwksKeyStore, require_admin

log = logging.getLogger("indexer")

Caller = Annotated[Principal, Depends(current_principal)]
IfMatch = Annotated[str | None, Header(alias="If-Match")]


# --- serialisation ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def project_json(p):
    return {k: getattr(p, k) for k in ("id", "title", "description", "members", "units", "created_at", "updated_at", "revision")}


def artifact_json(a):
    return {"id": a.id, "project_id": a.project_id, "artifact_type": a.kind, "revision": a.revision,
            "metadata": a.data, "created_at": a.created_at, "updated_at": a.updated_at,
            "file": {"filename": a.filename, "sha256": a.file_hash, "size": a.file_size} if a.file_path else None}


def with_etag(response: Response, record):
    response.headers["ETag"] = f'"{record.revision}"'


# --- lookups ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_session(request: Request):
    with Session(request.app.state.engine) as session:
        yield session


def get_project(session, project_id):
    project = session.get(Project, project_id)
    if project is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "Project not found")
    return project


def get_artifact(session, project_id, kind, artifact_id):
    project = get_project(session, project_id)
    artifact = session.get(Artifact, artifact_id)
    if artifact is None or artifact.project_id != project_id or artifact.kind != kind:
        raise HTTPException(404, "Artifact not found")
    return project, artifact


# --- PT1: optimistic concurrency via If-Match -------------------------------------------------------

def expected_revision(if_match: str | None, required: bool = True) -> int | None:
    if if_match is None:
        if required:
            raise HTTPException(428, 'If-Match header with the current revision (ETag) is required, e.g. If-Match: "3"')
        return None
    value = if_match.strip()
    value = value[2:] if value.startswith("W/") else value
    value = value.strip('"')
    if not value.isdigit():
        raise HTTPException(412, "If-Match does not match the current revision")
    return int(value)


def check_revision(record, expected: int | None):

        raise HTTPException(412, "The record changed since you read it; reload and retry")

def validate_metadata(kind: str, metadata) -> dict:

SAFE_FILENAME = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]")


def safe_filename(name: str | None) -> str:
    cleaned = SAFE_FILENAME.sub("_", Path((name or "").replace("\\", "/")).name)[:255]

def escape_like(value: str) -> str:

def write_encrypted(app, artifact_id: str, plaintext: bytes) -> Path:
    blob = app.state.cipher.encrypt(plaintext, artifact_id.encode())

    temporary = target.with_suffix(".tmp")
    temporary.write_bytes(blob)
    os.replace(temporary, target)

    path = Path(artifact.file_path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise HTTPException(404, "File not found")
    try:
        plaintext = app.state.cipher.decrypt(path.read_bytes(), artifact.id.encode())
    except DecryptionError:

        raise HTTPException(500, "Stored file failed its integrity check") from None
    if artifact.file_hash and hashlib.sha256(plaintext).hexdigest() != artifact.file_hash:
        raise HTTPException(500, "Stored file failed its integrity check")

def encrypt_legacy_files(app):
    """Encrypt manuscript files stored in plain text by the pre-hardening service."""
    with Session(app.state.engine) as session:
        legacy = session.scalars(select(Artifact).where(Artifact.file_path.is_not(None), Artifact.file_encrypted.is_(False))).all()
        for artifact in legacy:

            if not path.is_file():

            data = path.read_bytes()
            if data.startswith(MAGIC):

                    app.state.cipher.decrypt(data, artifact.id.encode())
                    artifact.file_encrypted = True
                    continue

                    pass
            new_path = write_encrypted(app, artifact.id, data)
            artifact.file_path, artifact.file_encrypted = str(new_path), True
            artifact.file_hash = artifact.file_hash or hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
            artifact.file_size = len(data)
            session.commit()

        session.commit()

                             max_concurrent_zips=max_concurrent_zips)

# Tool: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5)

# Prompt Summary: "Harden the PA2 indexer: local RS256 JWT auth, row-level authz, AES-GCM manuscript encryption, input validation, PT1-PT3 mitigations"

# Copy to .env (git-ignored) and fill in. Placeholders only: never commit real values.

# Host path of the PUBLIC JWKS file; mounted read-only into the api container.
JWKS_HOST_PATH=/absolute/path/to/jwks.json

JWT_JWKS_PATH=/etc/indexer/jwks.json
JWT_ISSUER=http://localhost:9000

MAX_JSON_BYTES=1048576
MAX_ZIP_FILES=50

MAX_CONCURRENT_ZIPS=2

# Optional host port for the api service.
PA2_PORT=8002
EOF

.env

!.env.example
*.pem

# Project Artifact & Repository Indexer (hardened)

FastAPI + PostgreSQL 17 service for projects and their artifacts (manuscripts with uploaded files, presentation videos, Git repositories). The PA3 hardening adds token authentication, row-level authorization, manuscript encryption, input validation, stale-update protection, an audit record and size limits. The functional routes are unchanged, except that updates now need `If-Match` (see below).

## Configure

Every variable is listed, with placeholders only, in [`.env.example`](.env.example). Copy it to `.env` (git-ignored) and fill it in:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `JWKS_HOST_PATH` | Host path of the **public** JWKS file. Compose mounts it read-only. |
| `JWT_JWKS_PATH` | Path inside the container where the service reads the JWKS file (default `/etc/indexer/jwks.json`). |
| `JWT_ISSUER` | Required `iss`: `http://localhost:9000` |
| `JWT_AUDIENCE` | Required `aud`: `cs763-api` |

| --- | --- |


# Task note: hardening the Project Artifact & Repository Indexer

Tool: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) · 2026-11-26 · Working folder `peer-artifact-indexer/PA2/functional-codebase/`

## What I was asked

Harden the PA2 indexer, which was built with no security requirements, and keep its functional behaviour. The requirements:

- Local RS256 JWT authentication from a JWKS file.
- Row-level authorization on projects and artifacts.
- AES-256-GCM encryption of manuscript file bytes.
- Input validation on every write.
- Fixes for CWE-306, CWE-862 and CWE-312, and mitigations for threats PT1 (stale updates), PT2 (no record) and PT3 (size DoS).
- Work test-first, and run the full suite both in-process and against Docker Compose.
- Update the README, add provenance headers, and write this note. No git commits.

## What I did

1. Read the existing code (`app/main.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, Dockerfile, pyproject, `../docker-compose.yml`) and ran the baseline suite: 11 passed.
2. Added the `pyjwt[crypto]` and `cryptography` dependencies with uv. Regenerated the hashed `requirements.txt` with `uv export`; the only change is four added packages.
3. **Wrote the tests first.** Test fixtures and a throwaway key pair (`tests/conftest.py`, `tests/keys.py`), then `test_auth.py`, `test_authz.py` and `test_security.py`, and updated `test_api.py`. Run against the old code: 11 failed, 158 errors.
4. Split the service into modules and implemented the controls (listed below), then rewrote the routes in `app/main.py`.
5. Changed Compose: read-only JWKS mount from `JWKS_HOST_PATH`, and the JWT, key and limit variables. Added `.env.example`, a `.gitignore` and `.dockerignore` entries.
6. Ran the suite in-process and against a Compose stack. Checked inside the container that files are encrypted at rest. Updated the README.

## Files created / changed

All paths are relative to `PA2/functional-codebase/` unless marked otherwise.

- **Created:**
  - App modules: `app/security.py`, `app/authz.py`, `app/directory.py`, `app/crypto.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/models.py`, `app/schemas.py`, `app/audit.py`, `app/limits.py`
  - Tests: `tests/__init__.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/keys.py`, `tests/test_auth.py`, `tests/test_authz.py`, `tests/test_security.py`
  - Config: `.env.example`, `.gitignore`
- **Changed:** `app/main.py` (rewritten), `tests/test_api.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `requirements.txt`, `.dockerignore`, `README.md`, `../docker-compose.yml`.
- **Unchanged:** `Dockerfile`, `app/__init__.py`, `fixtures/reference-data.json`.

## Weaknesses and threats: where each is fixed

| Item | Fix | Where | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **CWE-306** No authentication | Every `/api/v1/*` route depends on `current_principal`. Only `/healthz` is public, and `/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` are turned off. | `app/security.py` (`verify_token` 90-116, `JwksKeyStore` 45-87, `current_principal` 123-136); `app/main.py` `Caller` dependency | `tests/test_auth.py`: every endpoint returns 401 without a token, plus all the token cases |
| **CWE-862** No authorization | `can_modify` / `can_download` are checked against the stored project on every write and download; the audit log is admin-only. | `app/authz.py` 28-54; `app/main.py` lines 261, 275, 300, 335, 364, 378, 393, 419, 432, 449 | `tests/test_authz.py`; `test_auth.py::test_another_users_valid_token…` |
| **CWE-312** Plaintext files | AES-256-GCM with a random 12-byte nonce for each value and the artifact id as associated data. The hash is taken over the plaintext. Plaintext files left by the old service are encrypted at startup. | `app/crypto.py`; `app/main.py` `write_encrypted` / `read_decrypted` / `encrypt_legacy_files` | `test_security.py`: at rest, on return (single and zip), unique ciphertext, tamper detection, legacy migration, refusal to start without a key |
| **PT1** Stale overwrite | `ETag` / `revision` on every response. `If-Match` is required on PUT and upload (428 if missing, 412 if stale). SQLAlchemy `version_id_col` makes the check atomic in the database. | `app/models.py`; `app/main.py` `expected_revision` / `check_revision`; `app/audit.py` maps `StaleDataError` to 412 | `test_security.py` PT1 tests, including two sessions committing concurrently |
| **PT2** No record | `audit_events` table: actor `sub`, action, UTC time, outcome (`success`, `denied`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `rejected`, `error`) and status code. Covers project and artifact create, update and delete, upload, delete-file, download and zip. Refused and failed attempts are recorded. Each event is written in its own transaction and the table has no foreign keys, so events survive deletion. | `app/audit.py`; `app/models.py`; `GET /api/v1/audit-events` (admin) | `test_security.py` PT2 tests |
| **PT3** Unbounded size | ASGI middleware caps request bodies: uploads at `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` plus 64 KiB of multipart overhead, JSON at 1 MiB. It checks `Content-Length` and also counts streamed bytes. Files are read in chunks with an exact 413. The zip is refused with 422 above 50 files or 100 MiB, built one file at a time into a spooled temp file, and limited to 2 concurrent builds (429 with `Retry-After`). | `app/limits.py`; `app/main.py` `download_zip` | `test_security.py` PT3 tests, including a chunked body with no `Content-Length` |

## Decisions I made (and why)

- **A refused write returns 404 even though the project is readable.** Section 3.2 says a record the caller may not access returns 404. I applied that per action, so a non-member's PUT or DELETE gets 404 even though their GET of the same project succeeds. 403 is reserved for role refusals: a token with no known role (on every route), and non-admins calling the audit log. You could argue 403 is more honest for "visible but not writable". I followed the rule as written.
- **Membership can be edited through the project body.** `members` is project data that existing members or an admin may edit. The creator is added from the token's `sub` with role `creator`. The member `role` field in the body is only a label and never grants a token role (tested). Removing yourself is allowed, and at least one member is still required.
- **Faculty association is static mock data.** It lives in `app/directory.py`: a map from faculty `sub` to course and lab pairs. Only `course` and `lab` units count, not `department`, and the caller must also hold the `faculty_instructor` role.
- **PT1 uses `If-Match`, not a body field.** This keeps the existing request bodies unchanged. `DELETE` takes an optional `If-Match`; I didn't make it required, so existing delete clients keep working.
- **Zip size limit returns 422.** 413 describes the *request* body, so I return 422 with a message to download files individually. The zip limits are checked from the stored plaintext sizes before any decryption happens.
- **Limits:** 10 MiB per manuscript, 1 MiB JSON, zip at most 50 files and 100 MiB, 2 concurrent zip builds. All can be changed through the environment. The concurrency gate is per process, which is enough for one uvicorn worker.
- **Key format and startup:** `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is base64 of 32 bytes; standard or URL-safe base64 is accepted. The service refuses to start without a valid key, JWKS path, issuer and audience.
- **JWKS handling:** the file is re-read when its modification time or size changes, which supports key rotation. A missing or unreadable file means every token is rejected while `/healthz` stays up. Keys must be RSA, at least 2048 bits, with `alg` RS256 and `use` sig (or those fields absent). A duplicated `kid` is dropped rather than guessed. Any private parts in the JWKS are never loaded.
- **Compose and `.env`:** the Compose file lives in `PA2/`, so Compose's default `.env` would be `PA2/.env`. I kept `.env.example` and `.gitignore` in the working folder and documented `--env-file functional-codebase/.env`. `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `JWKS_HOST_PATH` use `:?`, so Compose refuses to start without them. Issuer and audience default to the configured values.
- **Seed data:** the service has none. `fixtures/reference-data.json` is not loaded by the app. Legacy plaintext files from PA2 volumes are encrypted at startup, and a small migration adds the `revision` and `file_encrypted` columns to existing PostgreSQL databases, because `create_all` does not alter existing tables.
- **Filenames:** uploaded filenames are cut to their base name and limited to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` (at most 255 characters). This prevents header injection in `Content-Disposition` and path tricks in the zip.
- **`requirements.txt`** got no provenance header: it is a generated, hash-locked export, which I treated like a lock file.

## Problems / things I couldn't do

- **Scope slip:** while first looking around I listed the `PA2/` directory and read `PA2/.gitignore`. Neither is named in 3.4. I did not open `security-analysis.md`, `sast-triage-report.md`, `.ai_logs/` or `evidence/`.
- **Audit gaps:** requests rejected before a handler runs are not in the audit record. That covers 401s (there is no verified `sub`), FastAPI 422 body validation, and middleware 413s. They are logged by uvicorn only.
- **Audit write timing:** a successful change's audit event is written in a separate transaction right after the change commits. If that write fails, the client gets 500 but the change stays. Putting the event in the same transaction would close that gap.
- **Key handling in Compose:** the encryption key reaches the container as an environment variable, as the brief asks, so it is visible to `docker inspect`. A Docker secret file would be stronger.
- **Database password:** the PostgreSQL password `local-course-only` was already hard-coded in the Compose file. I left it alone because it is outside the brief.
- **Skipped in Compose mode:** 8 tests need direct storage, database or app-state access and are skipped there. I covered encryption at rest by hand inside the container (results below).
- **Tooling:** `uv` and Python 3.13 were not installed on the host. I installed `uv` into the session scratchpad, and uv provided Python 3.13.
- **Not reviewed by a human:** nothing here has been reviewed by a human yet.

## Commands run / test results

- Baseline: `uv run pytest -q` gave **11 passed**.
- Test-first run of the new tests against the old code: **11 failed, 158 errors**.
- Final in-process run: `uv run pytest -q` gave **173 passed** (1 Starlette TestClient deprecation warning).
- Compose stack, run under a separate project name (`-p cs763-pa3-test`) with an image-tag override so the existing `cs763-pa2` volumes and image were not touched:
  - Setup: `python -m tests.keys <scratch>/compose-keys`, then `docker compose -p cs763-pa3-test --env-file <scratch>/compose-test.env -f docker-compose.yml -f <override> up -d --build --wait`. Both containers were healthy.
  - Tests: `PA2_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8012 TEST_KEYS_DIR=… uv run pytest -q` gave **165 passed, 8 skipped** (the in-process-only tests).
  - Manual check in the container: the stored file starts with `PAE1`. A plaintext marker was found in 0 files in the volume and 0 times in a `pg_dump`. Download returned the plaintext. `/etc/indexer/jwks.json` is read-only, and the container runs as uid 10001. 1164 audit events from 7 actors were recorded.
  - Teardown: `docker compose … down -v` and the test image was removed.
- Git: nothing committed, pushed or tagged.

**Status: done.** All tests pass in-process and against Docker Compose.

- **PT2 (no record):** a new `audit_events` table records who did what, when, and the outcome, including refused attempts. It survives project and artifact deletion. Admins read it at `GET /api/v1/audit-events`.
- **PT3 (size limits):** uploads are capped at 10 MiB, including chunked uploads with no declared length. The zip download is refused above 50 files or 100 MiB, and only 2 can be built at once.

**Decisions you may want to check:**
- **404 versus 403:** I applied "no access returns 404" per action. So a non-member who tries to update or delete a project gets 404, even though they can read that same project. 403 only means the caller's role isn't allowed the action at all.
- **Compose and `.env`:** the Compose file is in `PA2/`, so the service starts with `docker compose --env-file functional-codebase/.env up`. It refuses to start without `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `JWKS_HOST_PATH`.
- **Test stack:** I ran the Compose tests under a separate project name and image tag, so your existing `cs763-pa2` volumes and image weren't touched. I tore the test stack down afterwards.
